scope: Seven retained generic native histories: four calibrated-static 30 s repeated-bump records and three calibrated-static 4 s mixed records with identified actual lower k/c. No MATLAB process or new native case was launched for this screen.

recommendation.reason: A verified 32 V terminal envelope exceeds all seven exact mapped demands. A nominal 36 V supply is a candidate only if the chosen amplifier supplies at least this loaded envelope with the required 100 us current response; a 4 V drop allowance is a design target, not a guaranteed amplifier specification.
recommendation.31VException: Mixed seed 7 requires 31.1070685477 V at t=3.8701 s. Exactly one recorded 10 us sample exceeds 31 V; this prevents exact unclipped-history equivalence at 31 V but does not establish that force would fail at 31 V.
recommendation.higherBusMeaning: Higher supply voltage restores a missing delivered-voltage envelope. At a sufficiently supplied, matched 100 us regulator it does not change the configured bandwidth or force trajectory.

assumptions: Pointwise requested-voltage algebra only, not a real-coil native simulation or hardware qualification.
Generic requested voltage matches applied voltage because both native clipping flags are zero; the logged regulator uses the same limited current command.

All active current-unit feedback gains, holding/acceleration/guide feedforward and proper inverse current outputs, initial current and identifiedKf must use the uniform force-current transformation. Residual identified-to-physicalKf error is preserved.

The real winding has matched hotR/L/back-EMF compensation and the same100us current response. The modeled amplifier realizes the mapped terminal voltage/current without added phase, ripple or clipping.
Same upper-rigid prescribed robot-side kinematics and all original sensor, robot, guide and mechanical calibration. Actual finite robot impedance is not qualified.
HotRfactor1.39 corresponds to an assumed100degreeC copper rise. Temperature-dependentKf, Kf-versus-stroke, physical thermal response and safe supplier operating temperature remain unqualified.
31V usable output is a terminal-voltage envelope, not a guaranteed output specification from a36V supply.

The recorded generic normal-force errors remain source results. Equivalent real-hot force trajectories follow conditionally only if the entire current-force transformation is implemented and the mapped current/terminal voltage is delivered without additional dynamics or clipping.
The 31 V sample count is a sampled voltage-envelope check; it does not characterize the continuous-time pulse duration or the force error after hypothetical saturation.

The 32 V reserve applies to these seven retained histories. It is not an exhaustive continuous uncertainty guarantee, a larger-bump qualification, a winding thermal proof, or a measured hardware margin.
memoryScope: Seven separate short-lived reader processes previously loaded one native-history MAT at a time. This aggregation reads small JSON files, the 25 kB prepared-configuration MAT and streamed byte hashes; no native-history arrays are loaded.
